title: China plans standards for AI token billing
html:
Chinese President Xi Jinping during talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, 18 November 2026

China’s National Data Administration will improve standards for how AI tokens are measured, billed and checked for quality. The plan was set out in remarks by director Liu Liehong posted on the agency’s website on Saturday, Bloomberg reported.

Tokens are the small units of text, audio and video that AI models process. Chinese officials increasingly use them as a way to measure, and charge for, AI use.

An industry covering the production, sale and use of tokens is taking shape, Liu said, according to Bloomberg. So-called token factories are combining rented computing power, AI models and data to sell tokens as a service.

The agency said it will widen the uses for token services and work to prevent low-quality duplication across the industry.

Beijing has pushed the idea of a token economy all year. In March, Liu said China’s daily token use had passed 140 trillion, up more than 1,000-fold from early 2024, Yicai reported. By June, the figure had passed 500 trillion, according to agency data cited by People’s Daily.

Chinese firms have also started selling tokens to consumers, through banks and telecom carriers.

The agency did not say when the new standards would be published.

summary: China's National Data Administration will set standards for measuring, billing and assessing AI tokens as "token factories" spread.
